I strongly believe in working for the cause of strengthening the emotional health of persons with challenges and empowering women through outdoor sports and adventure activities. I also support persons from lower socio–economic strata and provide equipment to para sportspersons. I believe youth is the voice of tomorrow. So, we organise disability sports awareness and advocacy sessions at various schools and colleges. My goal is to contribute to create a society where everyone, regardless of ability, is treated with dignity and given a fair chance to succeed.

A student asks the speaker in the extract why she holds advocacy sessions in schools and colleges; which answer is correct? (A) Because she believes the young are the ones who will change how people treat disability. (B) Because she has been appointed to a vacant post in each of those colleges. (C) Because she wants to recruit para sportspersons for her own team. (D) Because she has given up competing and no longer visits schools.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: Because she believes the young are the ones who will change how people treat disability.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: Your school is to hold a disability sports awareness and advocacy session, and as Sports Captain you have been asked to speak at the assembly about it. Write a speech of about 100 words in which you give two reasons why students should attend the session.

markingPoints.description: Speech format: a greeting to the audience at the start and a suitable closing at the end
Content: states that a disability sports awareness and advocacy session is being held in school
Content: gives two clear reasons to attend, such as the work done for persons with challenges and for women in outdoor sports
Organisation: the ideas are announced one after another and the speech is broken into short paragraphs
Accuracy and expression: correct spelling, punctuation and clear spoken language

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
Good morning, everyone.

Our school is holding a disability sports awareness and advocacy session, and I want to tell you why it matters.

Deepa Malik, a Khel Ratna, Arjuna and Padma Shri awardee, organises such sessions at various schools and colleges. She works to strengthen the emotional health of persons with challenges and to empower women through outdoor sports and adventure activities.

She believes youth is the voice of tomorrow, so she wants us listening early. Her own life proves the point. Paralympics has given her a new lease of life and helped her push boundaries, and she says it made her realise that people with disabilities can be as capable as their able-bodied counterparts.

Do come, and be the voice of tomorrow.

questions.subject: English
questions.stem: The school magazine has asked you to write an article of about 100 words titled ‘Setbacks Are Stepping Stones’ on what a Class 9 student can learn from the example of Dr. Deepa Malik about facing setbacks.

markingPoints.description: Article format: a headline that sums up the message, followed by short connected paragraphs
Content: gives the example of the wheelchair verdict and the choice she made in its place
Content: explains that every setback is an opportunity to prove one’s own strength
Content: advises building a support system and believing in oneself so that obstacles become stepping stones
Accuracy and expression: correct spelling, punctuation and clear, simple language

answerScheme.modelAnswer:
Setbacks Are Stepping Stones

Dr. Deepa Malik was told that she would be bound to a wheelchair for the rest of her life, and she was paralysed waist down. She chose a world of limitless possibilities instead. Her example teaches us three things.

First, every setback is an opportunity to prove your strength, so refuse to treat it as an ending.

Second, surround yourself with a support system, because the support of her family, coupled with her own fortitude, turned her obstacles into stepping stones.

Finally, believe in yourself and let your journey inspire others. Physical limitations do not define a person’s potential.

My breakthrough moment came in the 2016 Rio Paralympic Games, when I secured the silver medal in the shot-put event. In hindsight, I feel it was a moment of personal victory and a step forward in changing perceptions.

(A) She believes she has changed every attitude and can stop competing now. (B) She believes the win moved people's thinking about para-athletes further than before. (C) She thinks the judges were unfair and wanted the scoring of the event changed. (D) She thinks she must change her own way of thinking before she competes again.

answerScheme.modelAnswer: She believes the win moved people's thinking about para-athletes further than before.

At 29 she was diagnosed with a spine tumour and underwent a surgery
The doctors then declared that she would be bound to a wheelchair for the rest of her life, paralysed waist down
She was given two choices, to squander her life in remorse or to transform it into a world of limitless possibilities
She chose to transform it and switched from swimming to para-athletics
